record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.original_question: What can be said about the model theory of the Laurent series field F_p((t))? In particular, is there a complete axiomatization of this valued field and is its full elementary theory decidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p be a prime number, let F_p denote the field with p elements, and let F_p((t)) denote the field of formal Laurent series in one variable t over F_p, equipped with its natural t-adic valuation v: F_p((t))^× → Z (so that v(t)=1, the valuation ring is F_p[[t]], and the residue field is F_p). View F_p((t)) as a structure in the language of valued fields (for instance, the three-sorted Denef–Pas language, or the language of rings together with a binary divisibility predicate for the valuation).

Determine the first-order theory of the valued field F_p((t)). Specifically:

(a) Provide an explicit, recursive (complete) set of first-order axioms whose models are exactly the valued fields elementarily equivalent to F_p((t)).

(b) Decide whether the complete first-order theory Th(F_p((t))) of this valued field is decidable, i.e. whether there exists an algorithm that, given a first-order sentence φ in the language of valued fields, determines whether φ holds in F_p((t)).
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability and a complete axiomatization of the valued field F_p((t)) is a long-standing open problem in the model theory of valued fields. Despite substantial progress on tame, separably tame, and Kaplansky valued fields, and partial results in restricted languages, no complete axiomatization or decidability proof for the full elementary theory of F_p((t)) is known as of 2026.
